rubrics.justification: The description is detailed and largely consistent with a 2AA blastocyst, including appropriate comments on blastocoel filling, compact ICM, cohesive TE, and intact zona. Minor speculative details such as exact clock-face positioning and subtle debris/irregularity are not clearly verifiable from the image, preventing a perfect score.
The response thoroughly integrates age, BMI, PCOS, ovarian response, semen parameters, endometrial thickness, first-cycle status, and lifestyle factors with embryo quality and prognosis.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear progression from morphology and patient factors to prognosis. Minor issues include somewhat overconfident quantitative adjustments and a few speculative links, but overall conclusions are well supported.

Recommendations are generally consistent with IVF practice, including SET for a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst and attention to OHSS risk in PCOS. Some suggestions such as ERA/endometrial microbiome testing after a single failed transfer are more controversial and not routine guideline-based first-line steps.

The response provides clear, practical recommendations for transfer management, luteal support considerations, OHSS monitoring, post-transfer follow-up, and contingency planning for future cycles with appropriate alternatives.
